subject: Quantive — dedicated pilot: GPU mix, TPS targets & next steps
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@quantive.ai>, Samir Rao <samir@quantive.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + ask: deployment mode and sizing inputs for dedicated pilot

Thanks again for the time this morning — good discussion and clear signals that Quantive wants predictable performance for the next pilot. Quick recap from my side and a few asks that will let us produce a tight dedicated sizing and a short cost/ops proposal.

Recap (short):
- Deployment preference: leaning toward Dedicated capacity with private networking/VPC (you mentioned compliance and audit logs).
- Primary workload: conversational search + long-form summarization for enterprise documents. Mixed request sizes (some short queries, some multi-thousand-token summaries).
- Current baseline: internal note that production traffic will ramp after pilot; initial steady traffic expected but with strong daily peaks.

Important inputs we need to finalize sizing:
1) TPS targets: steady-state (avg requests/sec) vs peak bursts (max requests/sec) — please give a 24h steady avg and a 1-hour peak number.
2) Token mix: avg input tokens, avg output tokens, and 95th/99th percentile tails (if available). Example: avg total tokens per request = 400, tail 2k+.
3) Latency SLOs: p50/p95/p99 targets (e.g., p95 < 300ms).
4) Model variants you plan to run (largest model + any cheaper embedding-only or reranker models).
5) Data residency / VPC / encryption constraints (confirm if on-prem is needed or VPC is sufficient).

I attached a capacity worksheet (quantive_capacity_worksheet_v1.xlsx) with a short table you can fill — if you return that we’ll run a ballpark mapping to GPU SKUs and share a follow-up call to review the numbers.

Next steps I propose:
- You: populate the worksheet with TPS and token profile (20–30 minutes).
- We: deliver a recommended GPU mix (H100 vs A100 vs cheaper accelerators), concurrency strategy, and a provisional cost sheet within 48 business hours of receiving the sheet.
- Quick calibration call: 30 minutes next week to review the recommended pilot footprint.

Thanks — I’ll draft an initial sizing once we have the token/TPS numbers.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
pri yom.das@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: quantive_capacity_worksheet_v1.xlsx (fillable), redwood-dedicated-estimate-20260714.pdf (placeholder)

From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@quantive.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + ask: deployment mode and sizing inputs for dedicated pilot

Thanks Priyom — appreciate the clear summary. Quick answers inline (we can expand in the worksheet but this should be enough to start a ballpark sizing):

- Deployment: Dedicated capacity with VPC peering. We do NOT need on-prem for the pilot, but must have customer-managed VPC and KMS-backed keys.
- TPS: Steady-state ~120 req/s (business hours). 1-hour peak observed during nightly batch/ingestion windows of up to ~600 req/s.
- Token mix: avg input 120 tokens, avg output 420 tokens (so ~540 total). 95th ~1.8k tokens, 99th ~3k tokens for long-document summaries.
- Latency SLOs: p95 target 350ms for interactive endpoints; background batch jobs can be higher.
- Models: Primary model is a ~13B family (custom finetuned), with a smaller 2–3B reranker and an embedding-only model used in parallel for search.

On cost: can you please include two-sided options — 1) lower-latency/high-cost GPU mix (for stricter p95) and 2) mixed GPU pool with cheaper accelerators for non-critical workloads?

I’ll populate the worksheet this afternoon and send back.

Olivia Park
Head of ML Engineering, Quantive

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@quantive.ai>, Samir Rao <samir@quantive.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + ask: deployment mode and sizing inputs for dedicated pilot

Thanks Olivia — this is very helpful. Based on the numbers you shared, here are two high-level sizing paths we’ll flesh out in the worksheet and the estimate PDF:

Option A — Low-latency / high throughput (single-tenant H100-forward):
- Target: p95 < 350ms for interactive endpoints.
- GPU mix suggestion (pilot): 2 x H100-80GB for serving the main 13B model (primary traffic), scaled with our smart routing to handle bursts.
- Purpose: H100 gives headroom for long sequences and larger KV-cache footprints; simpler to meet p95 targets with fewer nodes.

Option B — Cost-balanced mixed pool (H100 + A100 + cheaper accel for non-critical traffic):
- Pilot footprint: 1 x H100-80GB (primary), 1 x A100-80GB (secondary/burst), plus 1 x L4-class instance for embeddings/reranking and low-cost inference where latency requirements are relaxed.
- Purpose: route interactive traffic to H100 while batch/less latency-sensitive requests run on A100 or L4; reduces unit cost while preserving tail capacity.

Back-of-envelope token math (for planning only):
- With avg total tokens ~540 and steady 120 req/s -> ~64.8k tokens/s. Peak 600 req/s -> ~324k tokens/s.
- These are the numbers we’ll use to size batch windows, KV cache sizing and GPU memory planning; real throughput depends on quantization, model kernel efficiency, and batch behavior.

Concurrency and batching notes:
- We recommend steady concurrency targets per GPU (concurrency slots) rather than hard TPS caps; this lets our runtime auto-batch and keep latency SLOs.
- Suggested initial concurrency per H100 node: 18–28 concurrent requests (tune after perf runs). For pilot we’ll set conservative targets and run a perf sweep.

Next actions:
1) Please return the filled worksheet — we’ll produce a line-item GPU SKU mapping and cost delta between Option A and Option B within 48h.
2) We’ll schedule a 30-minute sizing review once we share the estimate.

I attached a provisional estimate (redwood-dedicated-estimate-20260714.pdf) with both options; the worksheet will make the numbers concrete.

If helpful I can also include a quick perf test proposal (2–4 hours of lab runs) to validate the GPU mapping against your actual finetuned model — this is our recommended next step before committing reserved capacity.

Best,
Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
pri yom.das@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-estimate-20260714.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Quantive — dedicated pilot: GPU mix, TPS targets & next steps

Quick internal note for the pilot recommendation (Priyom, sharing so you can present during the sizing call):
- Start pilot with mixed pool (Option B) unless Quantive is willing to commit to a heavier reserved H100 footprint. The mixed pool gives cheaper ops flexibility during tuning.
- Suggested pilot nodes: 1 H100-80 (primary), 1 A100-80 (secondary/burst), 1 L4-class for embeddings. If perf tests show the 13B model requires more memory/throughput, bump to 2 H100s.
- Ops ask: request request-level token distribution (CSV sample of 1k requests) from Quantive; this will let us run realistic perf sims.
- Can we also propose a 2-week perf validation window as part of the pilot contract? That should be in the proposal as a refundable validation credit.

I’ll pair with Marissa on the cost delta table (H100 vs A100 vs L4) and a runbook for graceful fallback (route to A100 if H100 is saturated).

Karthik
Director, Inference Optimization, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
